model_annotation: Figure 2 displays a bar chart titled "Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline Mistral-v0.2 and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data." The chart compares the negative log-probabilities of clinically relevant tokens across six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. Each group of bars represents one specialty, and within each group, two bars are shown: one for the baseline Mistral-v0.2 model (lighter shade) and one for the model fine-tuned on that specialty’s data (darker shade). The x-axis lists the specialties, while the y-axis represents the negative log-probabilities on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 10, ranging from 0 to 80. The bars are arranged in groups corresponding to each specialty, with the baseline and fine-tuned versions placed side by side for direct comparison. The chart visually demonstrates that for each specialty, the fine-tuned model exhibits lower negative log-probabilities (i.e., higher log-probabilities) for clinically relevant tokens compared to the baseline, indicating improved alignment with the target specialty’s terminology. The color coding is consistent across groups, with the same color representing the same model (baseline or fine-tuned) across all specialties. The figure illustrates that fine-tuning shifts the model’s probability distribution toward domain-specific terms, suggesting domain adaptation rather than mere knowledge injection.
